newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: NTMA says Ireland set for further debt reductions.
newsitem.headline: NTMA says Ireland set for further debt reductions.

text.p: Ireland's National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) said on Thursday that the state's General Government Deficit (GGD) dropped by 750 million Irish pounds in 1996 and the size of the national debt fell by 300 million - the first decline in almost 40 years.

"The combination of a low EBR and relatively favourable conditions in the Irish pound bond market facilitated the net repayment of some 1.0 billion punts (equivalent) in maturing and prepayable foreign currency debt in 1996," chief executive Michael Somers told reporters at the launch of the NTMA's 1996 annual report.
The NTMA said there was a 9.0 percentage point decline in Ireland's debt/GDP ratio to 72.4 percent at the end of 1996 from 81.4 percent at end-1995.
"This continued the favourable trend of recent years; a further reduction in this ratio is projected for the current year," Somers said.

In comparative international terms Ireland's GGD/GDP ranking improved by two places in 1996 and Ireland's ratio has now fallen to 98 percent of the EU average, down from 161 percent at end-1991, the NTMA said.

Ireland's custodian of the national debt said debt service costs were 67 million Irish pounds below the 1996 Budget estimate, this figure excluded an additional payment of 100 million to the National Savings interest reserve.
It said it had also made net present value savings of 57 million Irish pounds against an externally approved benchmark portfolio.

Ireland's General Government Deficit was 32 billion at year-end 1996 compared with 32.75 billion at end-1995, it said, noting that substantial positive foreign exchange movements helped achieve this reduction.
"These favourable foreign exchange movements have been eroded in the seven months of 1997 to the extent of some 440 million Irish pounds," the NTMA added.
It estimated Ireland's National Debt at 29.9 billion Irish pounds at the end of 1996 compared with 30.2 billion at end-1995.
Seventy one percent of that debt was denominated in Irish pounds compared to 65 percent at end-1995, it said.
Non-resident investors holdings, as a percentage of total outstanding bonds, rose 32.8 percent in 1996 from 28.6 percent in 1995 but fell back to 27.4 percent by end-June 1997, it said.
